archetype: Golgari sacrifice-and-recursion value deck with a reanimator opening: tokens and cheap ETB bodies die to free outlets, Meren returns one creature per end step, and fatties that pay on entering and dying are the payoffs. The audit established no archetype frame (base targets apply), and the goldfish_targets.json declaration still describes the September drain plan (Starscape Cleric, single-target drain), so its 0% rows are not a reading of this deck.
verdict: The deck functions: the turn-3 land drop lands 0.91 of the time, Meren is cast by turn six in 92.5% of goldfish games (median turn 4), and interaction is deep (18 copies, all five classes). What binds is engine speed: experience averages 2.433 at turn 6 and 4.266 at turn 7, so the fatties come back to hand rather than to the battlefield until roughly turn 8, and after the V29 and V30 cuts the early reanimator bridge rests on two cheap spells. Draw is the short axis behind it: one steady source (Sylvan Library), the rest on death, on mill or one-shot. No games are logged, and no swap weighed here (Haywire Mite and Eternal Witness included) is a clear upgrade, so the prescription is NO CHANGE until the first games say which exposure is real.

engine.declared: Tokens and cheap ETB bodies die to free outlets for experience; Meren returns one creature per end step (to the battlefield once its mana value is at or under the count, to hand otherwise); loaders and reanimation spells land a fatty before the counters catch up.

components.reading: Six free, unlimited outlets (Seer, Strider, both altars, Altar of Dementia, Yawgmoth), three tap outlets and four that cost mana and pay. Q050's 'outlets are thin' was written against the stale 4-card target group; by oracle text the outlet supply is deep.

Seven repeatable fodder sources, plus one-shot bodies (Woe Strider's Goat, Grave Titan's Zombies, Gisa's Zombies, Grist's Insects). Mean sacrifices are 1.343 by turn 6 in the goldfish, so fodder arrives but deaths are still slow early.
Loaders and millers are deep after V26; the yard fills faster than it empties.

Cheap reanimation that can land a binned fatty on turn 2-3. Cauldron of Essence (cast turn 3, first activation turn 4), Agadeem's Awakening (X-scaled) and Sheoldred are later lanes. The goldfish reads a 6+ drop out by turn 6 in 13.3% of games today; studies 008 and 009 recorded the V29 and V30 cuts each lowering it. A trade the pilot made knowingly for grind value.
Nine fatties that pay on entering, dying or each upkeep, and five death payoffs. Six drain cards are not modelled by the goldfish, so its turn-9 median kill does not read this side.

Experience accelerants: only Winding Constrictor multiplies; Toph, Yawgmoth, Cankerbloom and Karn's Bastion add counters. The goldfish's mean experience is 2.433 at turn 6 and 6.628 at turn 8, and it is a slight floor, since Cankerbloom's proliferate is not paid in the model. Before turn 8 Meren is mostly a regrowth engine.
Four pieces cover Meren against destroy; two (Heroic Intervention, Tamiyo's Safekeeping) cover targeted exile. No card in the 99 answers a counterspell since Veil of Summer left in V23.

single_points_of_failure.why: Meren, Cauldron, Reanimate, Animate Dead, Six's retrace, Jarad, Fiend Artisan and Hapatra's X all read our yard. Permanent hate is reduced, not answered: four instant-speed answers (Assassin's Trophy, Boseiju, Cankerbloom, Golgari Charm for enchantments) are four copies in 99, roughly 41% to hold one among 12 cards by turn 6 before tutors. One-shot exile (Bojuka Bog, Tormod's Crypt) is answered only by the self-returners (Reassembling Skeleton, Unshakable Tail with a Clue out, Jarad) and to-hand salvage (Takenuma's channel, Nyx Weaver). Jarvis's exposure (1) is real on both counts.

single_points_of_failure.component: Meren on the battlefield at end step
single_points_of_failure.why: The one-per-turn return is the engine's clock, so Meren is the hub. Her counters survive her death (they are the player's), so removal costs a recast at six and a tempo turn, not the pool. The insurance section says a hub justifies constant protection; the deck runs none (no Greaves or Boots) and holds two hexproof instants. Whether that is short is the section's own table test, unread until games are logged.

lean_into.why: With 2.433 experience at turn 6 and 4.266 at turn 7, Meren returns two- and three-drops to the battlefield (Cankerbloom, Satyr Wayfinder, Stitcher's Supplier, Formidable Speaker, Twilight Diviner, Unshakable Tail) long before a six-drop. Early, a fatty in the yard is a card to hand; a three-drop is a free re-fire.

gaps: No games are logged. Every exposure here is from card text and the goldfish; none has met a table.

Exposure (3), self life loss, is unmeasured. mana_analysis counts 8 life of one-time land costs and 3 per tap cycle from recurring lands; on top are Bitterblossom, Dark Prophecy, Reanimate, Yawgmoth, Sylvan Library and Malakir Rebirth. Eleven cards gain life (Zulaport, Cauldron, Meathook, Gray Merchant, Kokusho, Archon, Cavalier, Noxious Gearhulk, High Market, Scavenging Ooze, Tamiyo's Safekeeping). No artifact tracks our life total, so whether it costs games is for the log; the pilot's own note already says count life before a Dark Prophecy turn.

Exposure (6), piloting load, has no measure: one return a turn to choose, Twilight Diviner sequencing, Six's retrace, five unverified three-card lines and Dark Prophecy's life count. The first logged games are the only evidence.

Recon gaps, ranked by the inclusion rates recon records (2026-11-23), absent from the 99: Spore Frog 82% (cut V23 for the sacrifice-engine balance; a combat Fog loop), Eternal Witness 80% (cut V8), Victimize 71% (cut V29), Plaguecrafter 66% (an ETB edict loop), Accursed Marauder 61% (an ETB edict body; flagged, not pitched: its edict is symmetric, each player sacrifices a nontoken creature, and the pilot declined Braids as symmetric), Haywire Mite 58% (cut V17). Eternal Witness is a strong one: a three-drop Meren re-buys that regrows any of the nine instants and sorceries (eleven with the two spell-lands), which Meren and Six cannot reach. Not prescribed: `try` reads it for Woe Strider as slightly worse on what the goldfish sees (killed by T10 -0.7 pts [-0.9, -0.5], experience @T7 -0.07), and the spell re-buy has no measurement. Close, not clear.
No Forge run and no forge-cast-check on any card; the AI's handling of Meren's end-step choice is unaudited.

Haywire Mite, weighed and not prescribed. For it: recon's standout loopable artifact/enchantment answer, a fifth instant-speed answer to permanent graveyard hate, and `try --out "Woe Strider" --in "Haywire Mite"` (both seen, trust high) reads better on the binding axis: experience @T7 4.28 -> 4.40 [+0.10, +0.13], a 6+ drop out by T6 13.3% -> 13.7% [+0.2, +0.5]. Against: it is worse on damage @T10 (-0.1 [-0.1, -0.0]) and stall (+0.7 pts [+0.5, +0.9]); the gains are a cheap body the goldfish sacrifices, which Woe Strider's Goat and Skeleton already supply; and against Rest in Peace or Leyline of the Void it answers once but does not loop, since its sacrifice resolves while that hate still exiles it; it answers Tormod's Crypt only before Crypt is activated. Against Grafdigger's Cage, a noncreature artifact, it does loop: Mite exiles Cage, goes to a yard Meren can reach, and returns at end step for one experience counter. Cankerbloom (study 007, the pilot's pick) already fills the repeatable artifact/enchantment slot, and the pilot cut Mite at V17 for Constrictor and Toph. The Cage loop is real but narrow, one hate piece of four. The call stands on the rest of the case: a modest, mixed one-instrument read on a 0.12-counter margin, overlap with Cankerbloom, and the pilot's V17 cut. That is not a clear upgrade under the pilot's rule. If a logged game is lost to an artifact or enchantment graveyard hater, Mite for Woe Strider is the first swap to reopen.
